# Argus patches

`set_windows_software_rendering` records whether the application wants the Windows renderer on the system's software rasterizer, and `windows_software_rendering_requested` reads it. The flag is process-wide: the Windows platform reads it when it creates its DirectX devices and on every tick of its frame clock, so it can be set before the application starts or while windows are open.

On Windows, an unclaimed touch long press dispatches a right-button press and release to the existing context-menu listeners. Text selection and tooltip handlers retain first refusal, and the contact is claimed so releasing it cannot click through the newly opened menu. A release that first reports movement beyond the tap slop scrolls from the original contact instead of clicking its destination. Argus's `touch_input` regression covers taps, double taps, panning, cancellation, coalesced movement and claimed/unclaimed long presses.

Raw touch callbacks queue events during reentrant App updates and native modal loops, preserving contact order until the window can be updated. Consecutive moves from the same contact coalesce while queued; closing the window discards pending input. The normal path dispatches synchronously. Regressions cover cancellation followed by a new tap during a nested loop, and closing a window with queued input.

Resize notifications that re-enter while App is borrowed are coalesced and retried after the update, reading the latest platform size and scale. Uncontended resizes remain synchronous. This keeps saved-placement and maximized startup layouts aligned with the native client instead of retaining a clipped initial viewport.

Complete paints register decorative image and load-bar animation before presentation. Scene sorting remaps bar records to their sorted quads. `Window::invalidate_render_cache` requests a one-shot full platform redraw, used by isolated pixel comparisons.

In-scene area-filtered chart images can update their vertical extent through a retained bounds handle. Width, atlas identity, clipping and clean-scene checks still apply. GPU primitive value equality supports bounded static-prefix comparisons in the Windows renderer.

Completely clipped filtered images retain a decorative handle and the effective device-pixel mask. Translating within the clipped region needs no new paint. Entering the visible region, dirty views and expired handles request a full repaint.

`Window::paint_image_subpixel_in_scene` retains the bounds handle of a premultiplied image and marks it for composition with its actual backdrop before presentation. Windows shares the opaque-window request between its host and renderer at window creation.

Source: crates.io `gpui-pre` 0.3.12, based on Zed revision `d2a4fb6ded7c470be25d1541281da3882495b65b`. The upstream Apache-2.0 license and package metadata are retained.

The vendored package omits standalone examples and their media, the standalone benchmark, the package-local lockfile and the unnormalized manifest. The small EXIF fixture referenced by upstream source tests is retained. Source, build resources, license and upstream documentation remain available.

Local changes:

- Window display notifications try to borrow the app before updating it. Synchronous native placement changes coalesce into one deferred notification while the app is borrowed; a nested native message loop retries after the outer update releases the borrow. The update reads the latest platform display and preserves synchronous delivery when the app is available. `TestAppContext::test_window` is public for integration tests of native callback reentry.

- `Window::defer_presentation_until_layout` marks a measurement frame during prepaint. The compositor keeps displaying the previous scene until the scheduled draw has laid out the chart grid. The chart layer checks `Window::is_layout_only` before preparing textures.

- A retained scene records the physical bar geometry and source color used by the Windows compositor. Both render paths use the same leading-edge coverage calculation. An unchanged bar no longer requests a presentation.

- `Window::paint_image_subpixel_premultiplied` paints premultiplied BGRA chart textures with area filtering on Windows. Each image keeps its own pixel format throughout its atlas lifetime. Animated bars restrict their content masks to the reserved animation region, so background restoration covers the complete bar range.

- A position-only notification updates the screen-dependent state and notifies bounds observers without invalidating the entire local scene. Size and scale changes still use `bounds_changed`, including the explicit hidden-start viewport synchronization.
- Native caption hit testing uses the current platform pointer position against the last rendered hitboxes, rather than reusing the preceding mouse event's hit result.
- Paint-cache replay retains native window-control hitboxes along with cursor styles and input handlers. Cached title bars keep their drag, minimize, maximize, and close regions on every frame.
- `paint_image_subpixel` retains fractional device coordinates for continuously translated raster layers and clips through the existing content mask. Regular image controls retain their original pixel snapping. These images carry `PolychromeSprite::AREA_FILTER` in the sprite's former padding field, asking the Windows renderer to sample them by area; renderers that ignore it keep treating the field as padding.
- Decorative images and bars (optionally with rounded corners) can update their bounds in a clean presented scene. Handles expire on full draws, reserve fixed paint layers, and validate window identity, atlas lifetime, clip bounds and primitive type. Cached paint operations are updated with their corresponding scene entries; dirty scenes and interactions use normal drawing. Animated bars snap their sides and baseline to device pixels but keep a fractional top edge, drawn as a one-device-pixel coverage ramp (a vertical gradient), so their height changes smoothly instead of a whole pixel row at a time. The quad starts where the ramp starts, half a pixel above the top edge (but not above the bar's region), so its rounded corners move with the edge; anchored to the pixel row holding the edge, they jumped a whole row each time the edge crossed one.
- Scene revisions and the earliest animated draw order let renderers retain immutable pixels before the animated primitives. A complete paint advances the revision; the Windows renderer compares the static draws to retain identical prefixes or repair their changed regions.
- The runnable counter uses `AtomicUsize::try_update`, the current name of `fetch_update` on the workspace Rust toolchain. Ordering and checked subtraction are unchanged.
- Text measurement reuses matching wrap/truncation constraints and unwrapped text that fits the new width. Truncated or wrapped results cannot answer wider intrinsic probes. Line wrappers are acquired only for actual truncation, and decoration storage follows the number of style runs.
- Inherited text styles cache their resolved prefix, and text without background decorations skips the empty background paint pass.
- A scroll container's range runs from its origin to the far edge of its children plus the end padding and border, as CSS measures scrollable overflow (`content_end` in `src/elements/div.rs`). Upstream measured the children from the nearest one and left the border out, so a child placed before the content origin (an absolutely positioned overlay such as a scrollbar at the padding box) or a bordered container made content that fits scrollable by a few pixels and showed a scrollbar.
- Mouse-wheel notches (line deltas) animate with 100/3 px per line (`kScrollbarPixelsPerLine`), and cc `ScrollOffsetAnimationCurve` with the ease-in-out timing function and the inverse-delta duration (200 ms up to 120 px, 100 ms from 480 px). A notch during a glide moves its target and keeps the current velocity through an ease-in-out curve with an initial slope. The glide advances while the scroll offset is clamped during prepaint and requests animation frames only for the view being scrolled (isolated ones where the scroller's handle asks for them, `ScrollHandle::isolate_glides`). The innermost scroller that can still move in the wheel direction takes the event; outer scrollers leave it. `ScrollHandle::scroll_by_lines`, `glide_to` and `wheel_target` drive the same animation for elements whose own wheel handling applies deltas directly. Precise (touchpad) deltas and programmatic scrolls apply directly and end a glide. See `smooth_scroll` in `src/elements/div.rs`. Each glide offset, its last included, lies on whole device pixels (`Window::pixel_snap_point`): a glide moves the content by whole device pixels from frame to frame. A glide requests one more frame after its last step: what reads the offset while rendering, before prepaint advances it (Argus's pinned group header), would otherwise stay a step behind, and a whole-pixel step can be a pixel or two.
- `Window::report_moving_region` records a `ScrollRegion` in the scene: an id that stays the same while the content moves, where the content shows (its bounds within the current content mask, in device pixels) and its offset. Scroll containers report theirs while their offset is clamped; an application reports other moving content, such as Argus's entering page. The Windows renderer copies what only moved by whole device pixels (`scroll_copy` in its patches). `Shadow` compares with `PartialEq` for that renderer's scene comparison.
- Opt-in frame diagnostics report layout node counts, measurement time and cleanup separately; normal rendering does not enable the timers.
- A cached view rendering again only because it animates or because a view inside it is dirty replays the cached views nested in it whose cache keys still match; upstream renders all of them again. Only a view that was notified renders its nested cached views again (they may show its state), as does a window refresh. A nested view replays only if its ranges index the previous frame and neither it nor a view inside it was notified during the draw in progress. Each of its two ranges carries the number of the draw that recorded it (`prepainted`, `painted` in `ViewElementState`): a view that was prepainted and not painted, as under an element that is hidden, renders the next time it is painted. A view replayed whole is not visited, so the cached views inside it used to keep ranges from the frame they were last visited in: after any frame that replayed the window's content (a layer above it drawing alone, as the chart layer does once or more a second), the next change rendered every view of the window. A replay copies each of the last frame's lists entry for entry, so the ranges of the views inside move by where the copy landed (`rebase_nested_prepaint` and `rebase_nested_paint` in `src/view.rs`), and those views stay replayable. `Scene::replay` therefore records one operation for each operation it replays, including a primitive that was recorded inside a transform and is clipped out without it. A view drawn from a deferred element lies outside its view's range and still renders after a replay. `Window::request_animation_frame` marks its view for redrawing without a notification (`WindowInvalidator::invalidate_view_for_animation`): observers are not called, and the view counts as animating, not notified.
- `Window::request_isolated_animation_frame` (and `Window::request_isolated_view_redraw`) asks for a frame that changes nothing outside the nearest cached view around the view asking, the view itself if it is cached. The cached views further out, dirty only because such a view lies inside them (`Window::isolated_ancestors`), replay their last frame around it instead of rendering: each replays its prepaint and its paint in stretches, and between two stretches the outermost cached view on the way to an isolated view (`splice_holes` in `src/view.rs`) is drawn again where it lay, inside what it was last rendered and painted in (element ids, text styles, the views around it, rem size, content mask, opacity, and at paint the count of elements letting hover fills change in place and the groups around it for `group_hover` and the like), which its element state keeps (`SpliceContext`). A stretch stops short of the drawn view's use of its own element state, which drawing it again repeats: copied as well, the uses would pile up in every view replayed around it, frame after frame. The dispatch nodes a stretch copies stay open, so that the view drawn after it hangs under its node of the replayed tree (`StretchReuse` in `src/key_dispatch.rs`); deferred draws keep their parents across stretches, and the cached views inside the stretches move along as in a whole replay. Primitives keep their order: the stretches and the view drawn in place are recorded in the order of the last frame, and the transforms and layers pushed by a stretch hold for the view inside it. A view renders as before when it is dirty for anything else, when a view to draw again in it was not drawn inside its ranges in the last frame (`Frame::cached_views` lists the cached views whose ranges index a frame), when a deferred draw outside that view hangs from a node inside it, or while assistive technology reads the window (replays carry no accessibility nodes). A cached view after the drawn one in the same stretches replays even if the drawn view notifies it while rendering, where it would have rendered in the same frame; it renders in the next. `ScrollHandle::isolate_glides` makes a scroller's wheel glides ask for isolated frames, and `ScrollHandle::gliding` tells whether a glide runs (one whose scroller is no longer drawn stops counting once it would have ended): whatever reads the offset outside the cached view around the scroller must ask for its own frames meanwhile. Argus isolates its tables' glides; a glide frame draws the view of the table's rows (or the table frame, where the component draws the rows), and the page region for the process list's scrollbar, while the desktop around them replays. `ViewElement::following` marks a cached view that renders whenever the view holding its element renders, as an uncached view does: it shows state of the view around it, which changes without notifying it, and is cached only so that an isolated frame can draw it alone (`prepaint_view` skips the cache-key check for it; drawn in place by a splice it is handled as any cached view). Argus's table rows are such a view. `src-gpui/tests/view_replay.rs` covers the render counts, the element states a spliced frame uses (as many as a render), clicks in the replayed stretches and in the view drawn in place, a key bubbling from that view into the one replayed around it, and a following view rendering with the uncached view around it and alone in its isolated frames.
- `Window::with_visual_transform` moves and fades what is painted inside it without changing layout, element bounds or hit testing. The paint operations keep the untransformed primitives and the transforms (`PaintOperation::PushTransform`/`PopTransform`), so a cached view replayed inside a changed transform lands at the new place and opacity without rendering again; the primitive lists get the transformed copies, and draw order is computed from the transformed bounds. Glyphs, images and surfaces move by whole device pixels, where a fresh paint would have snapped them; sprite matrices absorb the move. Under a transform, primitives outside their clip are still recorded, so a later transform can bring them into view. `Window::with_visual_clip` adds a clip of the same kind: it narrows what is drawn without changing content masks, so a cached view inside replays under a new clip, where a changed overflow clip (part of the cache key) would render it again. Clips nest with each other and with transforms; a transform's own offset does not move its clip. `Window::with_live_transform` paints inside a `LiveTransform`: a shared value (a move, a scale per axis about the anchor it is painted with, a factor for border widths, corner radii, blur radii and underline thickness, and an opacity) recorded as its own operation (`PaintOperation::PushLiveTransform`), so every scene built reads the value again, replays of cached views included. An animation sets the value before each frame and draws without rendering the views it moves, as the page entrance does around a whole region, but for any part inside one. A device position `p` inside a transform is drawn at `p * scale + offset` per axis and nested transforms compose; a zoom scales border widths and radii with it (as a CSS `scale()` draws them), a stretch resizes boxes and keeps their borders. Scaled glyphs and images keep their exact place instead of moving by whole device pixels, so that they do not jump a pixel at a time while the scale changes, and are drawn with the renderer's linear sampling until it returns to 1; sprite matrices take the scale into their translation (exactly for unrotated sprites). A clip is not scaled by its own transform.
- With `ARGUS_GPUI_FRAME_TRACE`, `frame-phases` also carries the draw's end on the performance counter (`atQpc`, 100 ns, the window probe's clock), the time spent in view `render` calls, the number of replayed cached views, the views rendered and each view's own time per phase; `frame-present` records each present. Views are named by their types without module paths, generic arguments included (`short_type_name`): `Region<Page>`, `TableState<NativeTable>`.
- `Window::set_content_zoom` scales a window's content using Argus's interface scale: the platform multiplies its scale factor by the zoom and reports the content size and pointer positions in the zoomed coordinates, and the window refreshes its scale factor, viewport and pointer position (`bounds_changed`). Layout, painting, glyph and image rasterization, hit testing and the native caption hit test therefore stay in one coordinate space, at device resolution. The window keeps its size and position on screen. `PlatformWindow::set_content_zoom` defaults to doing nothing and must not call back into the window; only the Windows platform implements it.
- Line wrapping uses the CSS `normal` rules for Chinese and Japanese content. Upstream takes its break opportunities from ICU's line segmenter (UAX #14, `LineWrapper::break_indices`) with the default `strict` rules, under which small kana, `ー`, `〜` and `゠` may not start a line; the patch passes `LineBreakStrictness::Normal` with a Chinese content locale, as Chromium applies to `lang="zh-CN"` text with `line-break: auto`, and makes `break_indices` public so Argus can test its interface strings against it (`cjk_text_respects_punctuation` and `cjk_breaks_follow_the_normal_rules` in `src-gpui/src/frontend/theme.rs`; this package's own tests do not build from the published sources). The segmenter follows UAX #14 as of Unicode 15.1, which keeps `“` and `”` with the characters on both sides; the East Asian quotation rules of Unicode 16 are not applied. `icu_locale_core` is a direct dependency for the locale.
- Measured layout nodes can report their first baseline (`Window::request_measured_layout_with_baseline`), and text elements report the baseline of their first line where `paint_line` draws it: half the line height left after the line's ascent and descent, plus the ascent (an empty line takes its font's metrics, as a CSS strut). The leaf layout passes it to taffy as the node's first baseline, rounded to device pixels, below its padding and border. Flex and grid containers aligning items to baselines (`items_baseline`) then line up text baselines, and block containers take their first child's, as CSS does; upstream reported no baseline for measured nodes, so taffy synthesized one at the bottom edge and `items_baseline` aligned the bottoms of the boxes. Rounding keeps the fraction below each aligned baseline the same, so glyphs, whose baseline is rounded to the pixel grid when painted, land on the same row. Measured nodes that report no baseline behave as before.
- With `ARGUS_GPUI_COMPOSED_PRESENT` set, the Windows renderer shows each frame through a DirectComposition bitmap instead of flipping the swap chain (`present_composed` in `gpui-pre-windows/src/directx_renderer.rs`): the flat visual's content is a premultiplied `IDCompositionSurface` of the window's size, each frame copies the render target's dirty rectangles (all of it after a resize or a chart tree) into it and commits. The compositor always draws a bitmap itself, where it may hand a flip chain to a hardware overlay plane. The switch exists to tell the two apart on displays that show a translucent window's changing pixels brighter than a capture does; the default path is unchanged.
- A change of interaction state in an element draws the view that painted it again, without notifying it (`Window::redraw_view_for_interaction`): a hover or group hover style, a press and its release (the active style and the pending click that arms a drag), a tooltip coming or going, and the hovered range of interactive text. Upstream notified the view for a hover, which also renders every cached view inside it, and called `Window::refresh` for the rest, which renders every view of the window: a click anywhere, or a tooltip, drew the whole window twice. The cached views inside the redrawn view replay; their keys hold what they inherit from it (bounds, clip, text style and opacity). Starting a drag and dropping still refresh the window, since any view may style itself for the drag, and so does an element painted outside any view. An element that keeps no state (it has no id) has no hover listener, as upstream: its hover style shows when something else draws its view. Two things follow from views replaying for as long as nothing changes them. A tooltip found gone while the window prepaints it asks for its view again in the next frame; upstream's refresh does nothing during a draw, and the tooltip's request would stay in the view's replayed prepaint, laid out in every frame and shown at once if its element waited to show it anew. And an element's hover state takes this frame's hit test when the element is painted, for its own hover and its group's (`paint_mouse_listeners`): the listener compares the pointer's next move with what was painted, where upstream compares it with the pointer's last move, so that an element laid out or scrolled under a resting pointer is told when the pointer leaves it.
- Inside an element that allows it (`InteractiveElement::hover_fills_in_place`), an element whose hover style sets a solid background and nothing else takes that fill in place. Its background is painted as a quad the scene keeps track of (`Scene::insert_hover_quad`; transparent when the element has no background at rest), and the hover listener changes the quad's fill in the scene on screen and presents it (`Window::set_hover_fill`): no view draws again. The paint operation changes with the quad, so later replays show the same fill, and `Scene::replay` carries the quad's place along. The scene takes a new paint revision, which the Windows renderer treats as any paint that changed one stationary quad. The element is painted as before, and its view drawn again on a hover change, when anything lies over the hover style (a press, a drag), when the fill at rest is not a solid colour, or when its quad cannot be told apart from another in the scene. It is allowed element by element because code may count on a hover drawing its view again: a listener that sets state for the next render, or a render that reads the pointer. Argus allows it in its tables and in the details pane; what follows the pointer there asks for its own render (`tips` in `src-gpui`) or carries a hover style that is more than a fill (`icon_probe`). `src-gpui/tests/view_replay.rs` covers this, the replay of nested views, the unpainted view and the resting pointer; `scripts/ui-smoke.mjs --interactions` compares fills in place with a full paint.

- Follow-up presentations (`needs_present`), high-rate input coalescing and `Window::set_hover_fill` wake the platform frame source through `WindowInvalidator::wake_platform` and `PlatformWindow::schedule_frame`, so an on-demand Windows frame clock stays asleep when a visible window is idle and wakes immediately for scene-only updates.

The owned-window probe exercises normal startup, caption movement, resize, frame timing, and foreground isolation. Remove these patches when an upstream version provides equivalent behavior.

`Window::request_view_redraw` 允许在绘制之外只使指定视图重绘，沿用动画帧的失效机制，不通知观察者，也不连带失效缓存子视图。调用方必须为输入变化的子视图单独发送通知。Argus 在新快照到达时用它重绘桌面自身的元素树（状态栏）和进程页自身的元素树，并只通知内容随采样变化的区域；指针进出列表时也只重绘桌面自身的元素树。
